subject.title: fix(infra): make exec-approvals lock ownership filesystem-safe

question: Which open PR should be the canonical implementation for the exec-approvals VirtioFS lock leak, and should it first provide exact-head live runtime proof?
rationale: Both open PRs claim the same security-sensitive async/sync lock correction; choosing the lasting implementation and accepting its authorization-boundary semantics requires maintainer ownership judgment rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Adopt one canonical PR after live proof
options.body: Choose one branch, require redacted current-head runtime logs proving sidecar release and restored approval reads, then close the duplicate candidate.

options.title: Pause both pending a narrower owner-led design
options.body: Keep both proposals open only if maintainers want a shared lock-owner API or upstream dependency change before choosing a local implementation.

recommendation.title: Adopt one canonical PR after live proof
recommendation.body: Choose one branch, require redacted current-head runtime logs proving sidecar release and restored approval reads, then close the duplicate candidate.

likelyOwner.reason: Their production reproduction and overlapping implementation provide the clearest available context for comparing the two proposed fixes.
